title: Ghana's Digital Future: The Urgent Call to Design for All, From Day One
summary: The Internet Society Ghana is urging the nation's tech sector and policymakers to prioritize inclusive design for digital platforms, ensuring persons with disabilities are involved from the outset. This proactive approach aims to prevent technology from creating new forms of exclusion, instead fostering a truly accessible and equitable digital future for all Ghanaians.
content:
Ghana stands at a critical juncture, with its digital landscape rapidly expanding and poised for transformative growth. Yet, amidst this surge, a pressing concern has been voiced: the nation's burgeoning digital platforms risk leaving a significant portion of its population behind if accessibility isn't baked in from the ground up. The Internet Society Ghana (ISG) has issued a powerful call to action, urging developers and policymakers alike to integrate persons with disabilities (PWDs) into every stage of website, mobile application, and digital service design.

This isn't merely about ticking a box; it’s about fundamental human rights and unlocking Ghana's full digital potential. Exclusionary design—think websites incompatible with screen readers, apps with poor colour contrast, or platforms inaccessible via keyboard navigation—doesn't just inconvenience PWDs. It creates profound barriers to education, employment, healthcare, and civic participation, effectively carving out a new digital divide. As technology becomes increasingly central to daily life, these design oversights risk exacerbating existing inequalities and sidelining millions.

The solution, as passionately championed by ISG, lies in adopting a universal design approach. This progressive mindset means involving PWDs as co-creators, testers, and critical stakeholders from the initial concept phase, not as an afterthought. Such an approach not only guarantees equitable access but invariably leads to more intuitive, robust, and user-friendly platforms for everyone. Consider an app designed with clear navigation for someone with cognitive disabilities – its benefits ripple outwards, enhancing the experience for all users.

By proactively embracing inclusive design principles now, Ghana has the opportunity to set a global benchmark for digital equity and innovation. It's a strategic investment in human capital, fostering creativity and ensuring that the nation's digital future truly serves all its citizens. This move can prevent technology from becoming an architect of exclusion, instead transforming it into a powerful, unifying engine for nationwide progress and inclusion.
keyTakeaways: Persons with disabilities must be involved from the beginning of digital platform development to ensure accessibility.
Proactive inclusive design prevents technology from creating new barriers to access and participation for PWDs.
Adopting universal design principles leads to more intuitive and robust platforms, benefiting all users, not just PWDs.
author: JENNIFER AMBOLLEY
